title: Synthetic missing object-level authorization evaluation
vulnerability_name: authorization bypass through user-controlled object identifier
detection_method: pytest security test plus multi-file reasoning
why_code_is_vulnerable: The view_report function retrieves a synthetic report by a caller-supplied identifier and returns the report content without comparing the requester's identity against the report owner. Any caller who knows or guesses a valid report_id can view another user's object, so the authorization check is missing at the object level.
why_bandit_is_not_expected_to_detect_thi: Bandit does not flag this pattern as a high-confidence vulnerability because the authorization decision is implemented across multiple functions and data objects rather than a single obvious insecure API call or credential exposure. The missing check is semantic and requires reasoning about object ownership across the model, repository, and service layers.
expected_vulnerable_test_outcome: The functional test passes because the owner can view their own report. The security test fails because view_report('report-alice', 'user-bob') returns Alice's report content instead of raising PermissionError when the requester is not the owner.
final_repair_success_criteria: A non-owner cannot access another owner's report.
No new high-severity security finding is introduced.
